about.metaDescription: DevBox Tools is a free, privacy-first collection of developer utilities that run entirely in your browser — no server, no tracking of your data.
about.title: About DevBox Tools
about.missionText: DevBox Tools exists to give developers, QA engineers, and backend teams fast, no-friction utilities that respect their privacy. Every tool runs entirely in your browser — your data never leaves your machine.
about.privacyText: We do not collect, store, or transmit any text you type or paste into our tools. Analytics are limited to anonymous page view counts (Google Analytics) so we can understand which tools are most useful. No personal data is ever processed.
about.openText: All tools are free to use, with no account required. If you find DevBox Tools useful, consider supporting the project.

privacy.metaDescription: DevBox Tools privacy policy. Learn what data we collect and how we protect your privacy.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what data is collected when you use DevBox Tools and how it is used.
privacy.toolsText: Text, data, or files you enter into the tools (JSON, YAML, regex, diff, passwords, CPF/CNPJ, Base64, colors, and others) are processed locally in your browser and are never transmitted to our servers.
privacy.analyticsText: This site uses Google Analytics to collect aggregated, anonymous usage data: pages visited, session duration, geographic region (country/state), device type. Individual tool inputs and outputs are never included in Analytics data.
privacy.analyticsEventsText: We may track generic interaction events such as: tool used, result copied, export performed, language changed. These events contain only the tool name and action type — never the actual content you entered.
privacy.cookiesText: Google Analytics uses cookies and similar identifiers to distinguish sessions and measure traffic. The site also stores your language preference (NEXT_LOCALE) as a cookie. If Google AdSense is enabled in the future, it will also use cookies for ad personalization. You can manage or block cookies in your browser settings.
privacy.contactText: If you have questions about this policy, please reach out via the contact page.

terms.metaDescription: Terms of use for DevBox Tools. Free developer utilities provided as-is.
terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.useText: DevBox Tools is provided free of charge for personal and professional use. You may use these tools in your development workflow, QA processes, and software testing.
terms.testingText: Numbers generated by this tool are mathematically valid and have correct check digits. They are generated randomly and may coincidentally match a real registration. Use them exclusively in development, QA, and testing environments — never for real identification, registration, or any fraudulent purpose.
terms.warrantyText: These tools are provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. We make no guarantees about accuracy or availability. Use at your own risk.
terms.changesText: We may update these terms at any time. Continued use of the site after changes constitutes acceptance of the new terms.

cnpjAlpha.metaTitle: Alphanumeric CNPJ — What Changed and How It Works
cnpjAlpha.metaDescription: Receita Federal issued the first alphanumeric CNPJ (00.000.000/E08G-12) on July 31, 2026. Learn the new algorithm, validation rules, and how to update your systems.
cnpjAlpha.title: Alphanumeric CNPJ
cnpjAlpha.subtitle: What changed on July 31, 2026 — and what your system needs to handle
cnpjAlpha.backgroundText: On July 31, 2026, the Receita Federal do Brasil issued the first alphanumeric CNPJ: 00.000.000/E08G-12. This change is governed by IN RFB nº 2.229, published in 2024, which expanded the CNPJ format to support letters in any of the 12 base positions.
cnpjAlpha.whyText: The numeric CNPJ namespace was approaching exhaustion. By allowing alphanumeric characters (A–Z, 0–9) across all 12 base positions, the Receita Federal expanded the available registration space by many orders of magnitude. Both old numeric CNPJs and new alphanumeric ones coexist permanently.
cnpjAlpha.structureRootDesc: Identifies the legal entity. Can be numeric (legacy) or alphanumeric (new registrations).
cnpjAlpha.structureBranchDesc: Identifies the establishment. Can be numeric or alphanumeric. Official example: 12.ABC.345/01DE-35.
cnpjAlpha.structureCheckDesc: Always two numeric digits. Calculated using the same algorithm for both formats.
cnpjAlpha.algorithmText: The check digits use the same formula for both numeric and alphanumeric CNPJs. Each character is converted to a numeric value using charCode - 48 (not standard base-36):
cnpjAlpha.algorithmWeights: Weights for D1: [5,4,3,2,9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2] applied to positions 1–12. Weights for D2: [6,5,4,3,2,9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2] applied to positions 1–13 (including D1).
cnpjAlpha.algorithmRemainder: Result = remainder % 11. If remainder < 2, digit = 0. Otherwise digit = 11 - remainder.
cnpjAlpha.exampleText: First alphanumeric CNPJ issued (Banco do Brasil branch, July 31, 2026): 00.000.000/E08G-12. Verification:
cnpjAlpha.exampleOfficialFull: Official example with letters in both root and branch: 12.ABC.345/01DE-35.
cnpjAlpha.systemsTitle: What to Update in Your Systems
cnpjAlpha.systemsMask: Input masks: update patterns to accept A–Z in all 14 positions except the last two (check digits).
cnpjAlpha.systemsRegex: Validation regex: replace \d with [0-9A-Z] for the first 12 characters; keep \d for the 2 check digits.
cnpjAlpha.systemsDb: Database columns: CNPJ fields must be VARCHAR(18) (not INT/BIGINT). Store as text to preserve leading zeros and letters.
cnpjAlpha.systemsCase: Case handling: normalize to uppercase before validation. Store uppercase. Lowercase input is valid and should be accepted.
cnpjAlpha.toolText: Use the CPF/CNPJ tool to validate both numeric and alphanumeric CNPJs.
